newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Q1 business conditions improve y/y-survey.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Q1 business conditions improve y/y-survey.

text.p: Malaysian manufacturers reported an improvement in business conditions in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the same period in 1996, a survey by the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research (MIER) said.
The government-backed think tank said in a report released on Wednesday that its Business Conditions Index rose 8.8 points to 63.0 points in the 1997 first quarter versus a year ago.
Compared with the fourth quarter 1996, the index for the first quarter fell by 1.6 points.
The index measures eight components including expected production, current sales, capital investment and export orders.
MIER said that of the 175 manufacturing companies that answered the survey, 35 percent noted an increase in overall sales. It said that figure was the highest since the first quarter of 1996.
Manufacturers remained bullish about sales in the second quarter of 1997, MIER said. Of the companies surveyed, 55 percent projected better export sales.
The survey found that 93 percent of semiconductor manufacturers expected sales to rise in the second quarter.
More than two-thirds of the respondents expect higher production in the second quarter of 1997, compared with eight percent who are forecasting otherwise, MIER said.
The average capacity utilisation rate edged up by 0.7 of a percentage point in the first three months of 1997 from the fourth quarter.
Prices of locally-sold manufactured products stayed relatively stable in the first quarter, with 65 percent of the respondents having no changes in local sales prices.
Labour demand remained strong, as 28 percent of the firms surveyed said they recruited more employees, up from 25 percent in first quarter 1996.
It said 41 percent of the companies expected higher wage costs in the coming three months.

For all of 1997, MIER is projecting Malaysia's real gross domestic product (GDP) will grow by 8.2 percent, unchanged from the previous year. In 1998, it expects real GDP growth will rise by 8.5 percent.
